# General utilities

C's `<stdlib.h>`: allocation, number parsing, sorting, pseudo-random numbers and exit codes.

<h2 id="abs"><code>abs</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func abs(n: c_int) -> c_int
```

Computes the absolute value of an integer value.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/numeric/math/abs](https://en.cppreference.com/c/numeric/math/abs)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L39)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type    | Description         |
| ---- | ------- | ------------------- |
| `n`  | `c_int` | the value to act on |

**Returns**: the magnitude; the most negative value has none and the result is undefined

<h2 id="atof"><code>atof</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func atof(str: *char8) -> c_double
```

Converts a byte string to a floating point value.
Cannot report failure: a string that is not a number gives zero, and a value out of range is undefined rather
than reported. Use strtod, which reports both.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/atof](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/atof)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L48)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type     | Description                   |
| ----- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `str` | `*char8` | a null-terminated byte string |

**Returns**: the value, or zero when nothing was read; there is no way to tell the two apart

<h2 id="atoi"><code>atoi</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func atoi(str: *char8) -> c_int
```

Converts a byte string to an integer value.
Cannot report failure, and a value out of range is undefined rather than reported. Use strtol.

**Returns**: the value, or zero when nothing was read; there is no way to tell the two apart

<h2 id="calloc"><code>calloc</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func calloc(num: size_t, size: size_t) -> *var opaque
```

Allocates memory for an array of num objects of size and zero-initializes it.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/memory/calloc](https://en.cppreference.com/c/memory/calloc)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L80)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type     | Description                        |
| ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `num`  | `size_t` | how many objects                   |
| `size` | `size_t` | how many bytes one object occupies |

**Returns**: the address of the zeroed block, or null

<h2 id="rand"><code>rand</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func rand() -> c_int
```

Returns a pseudo-random integer value between 0 and RAND_MAX.
Nothing about the sequence is guaranteed, and it must never produce a key, a token, or anything an adversary
would like to predict. Rux/Random names its generators; Rux/Entropy reaches the operating system.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/numeric/random/rand](https://en.cppreference.com/c/numeric/random/rand)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L128)

**Returns**: a value in `[0, RAND_MAX]`, from a sequence that guarantees nothing

```rux
pub extern func realloc(ptr: *var opaque, size: size_t) -> *var opaque
```

Changes the size of the memory block pointed to by ptr to size bytes.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/memory/realloc](https://en.cppreference.com/c/memory/realloc)

| Name   | Type          | Description         |
| ------ | ------------- | ------------------- |
| `ptr`  | `*var opaque` | the block to act on |
| `size` | `size_t`      | a size in bytes     |

**Returns**: the address of the resized block, or null with the original still valid

<h2 id="strtol"><code>strtol</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strtol(str: *char8, endptr: *var *char8, base: c_int) -> c_long
```

Converts a byte string to a long integer, reporting where it stopped.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strtol](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strtol)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L151)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type          | Description                                                 |
| -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `str`    | `*char8`      | a null-terminated byte string                               |
| `endptr` | `*var *char8` | receives the address where parsing stopped, or null         |
| `base`   | `c_int`       | the radix, 2 through 36, or zero to read a C integer prefix |

**Returns**: the value, zero when nothing was read, or a saturated limit with `errno` set to [`ERANGE`](/docs/api/c/errno#erange)

<h2 id="qsort"><code>qsort</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func qsort(base: *var opaque, num: size_t, size: size_t, compare: func(*opaque, *opaque) -> c_int)
```

Sorts an array in place; the comparison must be a strict weak ordering and the sort is not stable.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/algorithm/qsort](https://en.cppreference.com/c/algorithm/qsort)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L203)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                              | Description                               |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `base`    | `*var opaque`                     | the first element of the array            |
| `num`     | `size_t`                          | how many elements it holds                |
| `size`    | `size_t`                          | how many bytes one element occupies       |
| `compare` | `func(*opaque, *opaque) -> c_int` | how two elements order against each other |

<h2 id="bsearch"><code>bsearch</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func bsearch(key: *opaque, base: *opaque, num: size_t, size: size_t, compare: func(*opaque, *opaque) -> c_int) -> *opaque
```

Finds an element of a sorted array; the array must already be ordered by the same comparison.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/algorithm/bsearch](https://en.cppreference.com/c/algorithm/bsearch)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/StdLib.rux#L214)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                              | Description                               |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `key`     | `*opaque`                         | the value to search for                   |
| `base`    | `*opaque`                         | the first element of the array            |
| `num`     | `size_t`                          | how many elements it holds                |
| `size`    | `size_t`                          | how many bytes one element occupies       |
| `compare` | `func(*opaque, *opaque) -> c_int` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: the address of a matching element, or null

<h2 id="rand-max"><code>RAND_MAX</code></h2>

```rux
// Windows
pub const RAND_MAX: int32 = 32767;

// Linux · macOS · FreeBSD
pub const RAND_MAX: int32 = 2147483647;
```

`RAND_MAX`: the largest value [`rand`](/docs/api/c/stdlib#rand) can return on this target.
